original_test_intent: Demonstrate that supported Common Refcode Configuration controls accept approved non-default values, survive save/reboot, and return to the recipe defaults after Load Defaults without corrupting early platform initialization, device enumeration or boot health.
original_method: Capture motherboard/CPU/memory/PCIe population, BIOS/reference-code build and every scoped Common Refcode default; retain pre-existing logs with a timestamp marker; choose a minimal dependency-aware reversible matrix and change one control/group per checkpoint through KVM; record page values, save, reboot and verify POST plus CPU/memory/PCIe/UPI/device inventory before confirming retention; invoke Load Defaults and repeat the same inventory/default comparison; stop on initialization or enumeration drift and use owner-controlled known-good/CMOS recovery without automatic attempts.
manual_activity: A qualified operator uses the approved BIOS console/KVM to modify only the authorized Common Refcode controls, saves/reboots at controlled checkpoints, captures screens and applies Load Defaults; physical recovery remains available.
required_inputs: Motherboard, CPU, memory and PCIe population plus BIOS/reference-code build and exact page path
Complete SPEC default oracle and safe non-default matrix including dependencies and expected initialization effects
POST/readiness timing and CPU/memory/UPI/PCIe/critical-device inventory oracle
KVM/maintenance approval, last-known-good settings, recovery/CMOS ownership and escalation path
safety_requirements: Do not execute all/random settings; qualify each Common Refcode control, dependency and expected hardware effect
Preserve SEL/kernel/system evidence and use time markers instead of clearing logs
Checkpoint platform inventory after every saved change; do not continue after missing memory, link, socket or critical device
Keep BMC/KVM and physical recovery available before save; never assume Load Defaults restores vendor/project overrides
No automatic reboot, retry or CMOS clear
agent_execution_scope: Verify identity, refcode build, default/value matrix, dependencies, inventory oracle, maintenance and recovery
Guide manual checkpoints and collect page screenshots, POST/boot timing, hardware enumeration and log deltas
Compare retained and restored settings/inventory with SPEC without issuing a DUT verdict
Do not choose settings, clear logs, manipulate BIOS/CMOS or initiate blind recovery
engineer_actions: Approve Common Refcode page/revision, every default and the minimal reversible non-default/dependency matrix
Approve hardware-inventory and error acceptance, reboot/readiness limits, Load-Defaults scope and recovery
Review page, POST, inventory and log evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH MANUAL COMMON-REFCODE INITIALIZATION PERSISTENCE AND DEFAULT-RESTORE TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a minimal dependency-aware matrix and validate page state plus full early-initialization hardware inventory at every saved-change and restore checkpoint.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds reference-code revision, cross-subsystem inventory, incremental isolation, preserved evidence and controlled recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A setting can persist visually yet alter memory training, UPI/PCIe enumeration or other early-init behavior; checking only the BIOS page and eventual boot would miss that regression.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Common refcode knobs may act before OS logging and can cause training delays, device loss, POST hang or no-boot across several subsystems.

project_override_considerations: Project recipe defaults may differ from silicon-vendor defaults; the authoritative oracle and Load-Defaults behavior must distinguish them. If Load Defaults overwrites unrelated project settings, the owner must approve snapshot/restoration scope.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approval and platform/BIOS/reference-code identity
SPEC/project default oracle, safe matrix, dependency and expected-effect rationale
Baseline, changed, retained, Load-Defaults and restored page screenshots with timestamps
POST/readiness and CPU/memory/UPI/PCIe/critical-device inventory comparison after each reboot
Preserved BMC/SEL/kernel/system logs and unexplained-delta analysis

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2177 Wistron-BIOS-00494-V004: approve platform/BIOS/reference-code identity, exact Common Refcode page and SPEC/project defaults; safe minimal reversible values and dependencies replacing `all/random`; POST plus CPU/memory/UPI/PCIe/critical-device inventory criteria, reboot/error limits, log preservation, Load-Defaults scope, aborts, and KVM/physical/CMOS recovery ownership.

review_improvement: Adds the early-initialization and cross-subsystem evidence unique to Common Refcode controls, preventing a visually retained setting from hiding memory/link/device regressions and avoiding unrecoverable random combinations.
independent_technical_reasoning: Common reference-code settings are consumed during firmware initialization, often before OS diagnostics exist. A boot that eventually reaches setup is insufficient if memory capacity, UPI, PCIe or critical devices changed. Therefore each approved setting checkpoint needs both screen-state proof and a defined hardware-inventory comparison. The all/random instruction is especially unsafe here because interacting low-level controls can produce opaque no-boot failures; manual, incremental execution with physical recovery is required.
